The patient has irritable bowel syndrome, which involves the colon. Sympathetic preganglionic neurons for the gut arise in the thoracolumbar cord (T10–L2). The team note, though, says the answer is one of the lumbosacral options, and L3–L5 fits the lower gut better than S2–S4, since S2–S4 is parasympathetic (pelvic splanchnic nerves). I'm choosing **L3–L5**, but that choice rests on the team note, not on my own anatomy. By standard anatomy the sympathetic outflow is T10–L2 (the lumbar splanchnic nerves to the hindgut are L1–L2), so my earlier answer still stands on its own reasoning.
